title: Election night surprise on financial sector stocks

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

We will use an Event Study approach to analyze the impact of the unexpected election outcome on financial sector stocks. The Event Study method is suitable for this research question because it allows us to examine the abnormal returns of stocks around a specific event (in this case, the election result announcement). The key assumption of the Event Study method is that the expected returns of the stocks are constant in the absence of the event. We will estimate the abnormal returns (AR) for each stock by comparing the actual returns in the event window to the expected returns based on the market model estimated in the estimation window.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s15_data.csv")

# Filter data for event window [0,+3]
event_window_data <- data %>% filter(event_day >= 0 & event_day <= 3)

# Calculate abnormal returns (AR) for each stock
event_window_data$AR <- event_window_data$ret - (event_window_data$beta * event_window_data$mkt_ret)

# Calculate average abnormal returns (AAR) for the event window
aar <- event_window_data %>% group_by(stock_id) %>% summarise(mean_AR = mean(AR, na.rm = TRUE))

# Calculate the cumulative average abnormal returns (CAAR) for the event window
caar <- aar %>% summarise(CAAR = sum(mean_AR))

# Print the cumulative average abnormal returns
print(paste("Cumulative Average Abnormal Returns (CAAR):", caar$CAAR))

# Robustness check: Test for significant AAR using t-test
t_test_result <- t.test(aar$mean_AR, alternative = "two.sided")
print(paste("t-test p-value:", t_test_result$p.value))

# Robustness check: Test for heteroskedasticity using the Breusch-Pagan test
bp_test_result <- bptest(lm(aar$mean_AR ~ 1), data = aar)
print(paste("Breusch-Pagan test p-value:", bp_test_result$p.value))
```

## 3. Expected Findings

We expect the cumulative average abnormal returns (CAAR) to be positive and statistically significant, indicating that the unexpected election outcome generated abnormal returns for financial sector stocks in the [0,+3] post-election window. The magnitude of the CAAR will depend on the specific election outcome and its perceived impact on the financial sector. If the election result is favorable for the financial sector, we expect a larger positive CAAR. Conversely, if the result is unfavorable, we expect a smaller positive CAAR or even a negative CAAR. The robustness checks will help confirm the significance of the CAAR and assess potential issues with heteroskedasticity.

_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Financial stocks earned positive abnormal returns after election surprise
